title: Cherry Tree
statementMd:
You are given a rooted tree with $n$ vertices$^{\text{∗}}$. The vertices of the tree are numbered with integers from $1$ to $n$. The root of the tree is vertex number $1$.

In each leaf$^{\text{†}}$ of the tree, there grows one cherry. You want to collect all the cherries, and to do this, you perform the following action several times:

You choose any vertex of the tree $v$ (including the root or a leaf) and "shake" it. After that, cherries fall from all the leaves that are descendants$^{\text{‡}}$ of vertex $v$ (if vertex $v$ itself is a leaf, then a cherry falls from it). If cherries have already fallen from any leaf before, the tree will break, so such a situation must be avoided.

According to an ancient legend of the cherry orchard, the number of vertices you shake should be a multiple of three.

Is it possible to collect all the cherries in this way?

$^{\text{∗}}$A tree with $n$ vertices is an undirected connected graph with $n$ vertices and $n - 1$ edges. A rooted tree is a tree in which one of the vertices is special and is called the root.

$^{\text{†}}$A leaf is a vertex that has no descendants.

$^{\text{‡}}$The descendants of vertex $v$ are all vertices $u \neq v$ such that on the shortest path from the root to $u$, vertex $v$ is encountered.

## Input

Each test consists of several test cases. The first line contains a single integer $t$ $(1 \le t \le 10^4)$ — the number of test cases. The following lines describe the test cases.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer $n$ ($2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$).

The next $n - 1$ lines of each test case contain two integers $u$ and $v$ ($1 \leq u, v \leq n, u \neq v$) — the vertices connected by the next edge of the tree.

It is guaranteed that the graph in each data set is a tree.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ across all input data sets does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each input data set, output "`YES`" on a separate line if it is possible to collect all the cherries. Otherwise, output "`NO`".

You can print each letter in any case (upper or lower). For example, "`YeS`", "`no`" and "`yES`" are all acceptable.

## Note

In the first test case, you can shake vertices $2, 3, 4$.

In the second test case, the only way to shake a number of vertices that is a multiple of three is to shake all the vertices. However, doing so would break the tree, so this is not allowed.

In the third test case, you can, for example, shake vertices $2, 7, 9$.
statementZhMd:
给你一棵有 $n$ 个顶点的有根树$^{\text{∗}}$。树的顶点用 $1$ 到 $n$ 的整数编号。树的根是编号为 $1$ 的顶点。

树的每个叶子$^{\text{†}}$上都长着一颗樱桃。你想收集所有的樱桃，为此需要执行以下操作若干次：

你选择树上的任意一个顶点 $v$（包括根或叶子）并“摇晃”它。之后，所有作为顶点 $v$ 的后代$^{\text{‡}}$的叶子上的樱桃都会掉落（如果顶点 $v$ 本身就是叶子，那么会有一颗樱桃从它上面掉落）。如果某个叶子上的樱桃之前已经掉落过，树就会折断，因此必须避免这种情况。

根据樱桃园的古老传说，你摇晃的顶点数量应当是三的倍数。

你能否通过这种方式收集到所有樱桃？

$^{\text{∗}}$具有 $n$ 个顶点的树是一个含有 $n$ 个顶点和 $n - 1$ 条边的无向连通图。有根树是指其中一个顶点较为特殊、被称为根的树。

$^{\text{†}}$叶子是没有后代的顶点。

$^{\text{‡}}$顶点 $v$ 的后代是指所有满足以下条件的顶点 $u \neq v$：在从根到 $u$ 的最短路径上会经过顶点 $v$。

## 输入格式

每个测试由若干个测试用例组成。第一行包含一个整数 $t$ $(1 \le t \le 10^4)$——测试用例的数量。接下来的各行描述这些测试用例。

每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $n$ ($2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$)。

每个测试用例接下来的 $n - 1$ 行各包含两个整数 $u$ 和 $v$ ($1 \leq u, v \leq n, u \neq v$)——表示树的一条边所连接的两个顶点。

保证每组输入数据中的图是一棵树。

保证所有输入数据组的 $n$ 之和不超过 $2 \cdot 10^5$。

## 输出格式

对于每组输入数据，如果可以收集到所有樱桃，则在单独的一行输出“`YES`”；否则输出“`NO`”。

输出的每个字母可以用任意大小写（大写或小写）。例如，“`YeS`”、“`no`”和“`yES`”都是可以接受的。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，你可以摇晃顶点 $2, 3, 4$。

在第二个测试用例中，摇晃三的倍数个顶点的唯一方式是摇晃所有顶点。然而这样做会使树折断，因此是不被允许的。

在第三个测试用例中，例如你可以摇晃顶点 $2, 7, 9$。
